============================================================
Empirical Research Plan
============================================================

1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with staggered adoption, augmented by an event-study specification.

Why it fits:
•  The treatment—the passage of state anti-takeover laws (ATLs)—occurs at different calendar years across states but is common to every incorporated firm within a state once enacted.  
•  Firms incorporated in non-adopting states (or pre-treatment years of adopting states) supply a plausible counterfactual path for treated firms.  
•  Laws are written and voted on by state legislatures, largely exogenous to any single publicly traded firm’s contemporaneous performance, satisfying the quasi-experiment intuition.  
•  A dynamic event study (leads/lags) lets us (i) test pre-treatment parallel-trend assumptions and (ii) trace the full adjustment path of managerial behaviour and firm performance.

To avoid bias from heterogeneous treatment timing under two-way fixed effects (TWFE), I will implement newer estimators (Callaway-Sant’Anna, Sun-Abraham, or Gardner) that recover cohort-specific effects and then aggregate.

2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
  •  Treated_it = 1 if firm i is incorporated in state s whose first ATL becomes effective by year t and t ≥ effective year; 0 otherwise.

Control group (counterfactual)  
  •  (a) Firms incorporated in states that never pass an ATL during 1980-1995.  
  •  (b) Pre-treatment observations of eventually treated states (i.e., Goodman-Bacon decomposition compliant).  

Treatment timing / event date  
  •  First effective date of any ATL in a firm’s incorporation state. (Event time τ = 0 in that year; τ = −k and +k for leads/lags.)

No running variable—RDD not required.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends: Absent ATLs, performance trajectories of treated and control firms would have moved in parallel.  
  •  Plausibility: States introduced ATLs mainly in reaction to national hostile-takeover activity, not because of declining in-state firm performance, making the assumption credible but testable.  

A2. No Anticipation: Firms do not materially change behaviour before the effective date (or announcement date if earlier).  
  •  Plausibility: Legislative processes are slow and somewhat predictable but exact passage timing is uncertain; event-study leads will empirically assess anticipation.  

A3. SUTVA / No Cross-State Spillovers: An ATL in state s affects only firms incorporated in s.  
  •  Plausibility: Managers could re-incorporate in Delaware, creating spillovers. We will track reincorporation and check robustness excluding migrators.  

A4. Exogeneity of Treatment Timing: The calendar year a state adopts an ATL is not chosen in response to contemporaneous performance of its publicly traded firms.  
  •  Plausibility: Political variables (party control, lobbying intensity) dominate timing; will control for state-year covariates to bolster.  

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigations
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential Pre-Trends  
  •  Mitigation: Include firm and year fixed effects, state-specific linear trends, and inspect event-study leads; drop or re-weight cohorts failing pre-trend tests.

T2. Concurrent State-Level Shocks (e.g., tax reforms, recessions)  
  •  Mitigation: Control for state-year macro covariates (GDP growth, unemployment, unionization laws). Also add state-by-industry trends or use stacked-DiD that drops each cohort’s never-treated comparison after treatment.

T3. Selection via Re-incorporation  
  •  Mitigation: Obtain historical incorporation data (e.g., Compustat header). Create dummy for reincorporation; (i) control for it, (ii) test effects on stable incorporators only, (iii) instrument actual reincorporation with ATL status if necessary.

5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#-----------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#-----------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)          # fast high-dim FE
library(did)             # Callaway-Sant’Anna
library(did2s)           # Sun-Abraham helper
library(ggplot2)

#-----------------------------------------------
# 1. Load & Merge
#-----------------------------------------------
dt  <- fread("firm_panel_1980_1995.csv")        # firm-year info
atl <- fread("state_ATL_effective_dates.csv")   # state, first_effective_year

#-----------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct Treatment & Event Time
#-----------------------------------------------
dt   <- merge(dt, atl, by = "state_inc", all.x = TRUE)
dt[, treat_year  := first_effective_year]                 # NA = never treated
dt[, treated      := !is.na(treat_year)]
dt[, g            := treat_year]                          # cohort
dt[, post         := ifelse(!is.na(treat_year) & year >= treat_year, 1, 0)]

# Event-time variable for event study
dt[, tau := year - treat_year]                            # tau = NA for never-treated

#-----------------------------------------------
# 3. Main Specification (C-S estimator)
#-----------------------------------------------
cs_out <- att_gt(yname  = "ROA",
                 tname  = "year",
                 idname = "permno",          # unique firm id
                 gname  = "g",               # cohort
                 xformla = ~ size + leverage + industry_fe,   # optional controls
                 data   = dt,
                 est_method = "dr",
                 clustervars = "state_inc")  # cluster at state level

agg_effect <- aggte(cs_out, type = "group")   # aggregate ATT
summary(agg_effect)

#-----------------------------------------------
# 4. Event-Study (Sun & Abraham via did2s)
#-----------------------------------------------
es_out <- did2s(data = dt[treated == TRUE | is.na(treat_year)],  # keep both
                yname = "ROA",
                first_stage = ~ 0 | permno + year,               # firm & year FE
                second_stage = ~ i(tau, treated, ref = -1),      # ref. year −1
                cluster_var = "state_inc")
summary(es_out)

#-----------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness: Add State-Specific Linear Trends
#-----------------------------------------------
dt[, st_trend := year * as.numeric(as.factor(state_inc))]

robust <- feols(ROA ~ post + size + leverage | permno + year + state_inc[year], 
                data = dt, cluster = ~state_inc)
summary(robust)
```
(Replace ROA with other outcomes such as stock-return measures; swap fixed effects accordingly.)

6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (agency costs, managerial entrenchment) predicts that protecting managers from the market for corporate control reduces performance discipline.

Prior:  
•  Return on Assets (ROA) – decline of roughly 1 – 1.5 percentage points (≈ 5-10 % of mean ROA).  
•  Stock-market risk-adjusted returns – cumulative abnormal return around −2 % to −4 % in the five years post-ATL.  
•  Managerial behaviour – higher cash holdings, lower payout, more empire-building investments.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
------------------------------------------------------------
C1. Parallel-trend evidence (pre-treatment flat, p > 0.10) ………………… 1  
C2. No anticipation (no statistically sig. τ = −2, −3) …………………………… 1  
C3. No spillovers / SUTVA holds ………………………………………………………… 0.5 (re-incorporation risk)  
C4. Treatment timing exogenous to outcomes …………………………………… 0.5 (possible lobbying)  
C5. Correct estimator for staggered adoption …………………………………… 1  

Overall score: 4 / 5 – credible but not bullet-proof; robustness checks essential.

============================================================
